docs.title: ERGO × Microsoft Female Leadership Workshop
docs.text:
×

Welcome! In this hands-on session you will use Microsoft 365 Copilot custom skills. A skill is a short set of instructions that tells Copilot how your team does a recurring task. Once the skill is added, you simply ask in plain language and Copilot applies your method.

There are two labs. Pick one to start with; each takes about 15 minutes.

P1PowerPoint Prepare a committee decision check

Turn a dense proposal slide into one clear decision slide for the committee.

This way to PowerPoint → X1Excel Find launch blockers in a register

Turn a 24-item pilot register into a formula-based launch review.

This way to Excel →

docs.title: What you will practise
docs.text:
• Add a custom skill and read what it tells Copilot to do
  • Ask for the task normally, without naming the skill
  • Check that the result matches what you expected
  • Decide what still needs human judgement

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot in PowerPoint or Excel for the web
  • The practice file and skill package, downloadable inside each lab
  • Permission to edit the file you open

Workshop data

All numbers, names and records are fictional and were created for this workshop. They are not ERGO operating data.

docs.title: Lab P1 - Prepare a committee decision check
docs.text:
In this lab you will add a custom skill to Copilot in PowerPoint. Then you will ask for a committee readiness check in plain language. Copilot will add one clear final slide to a fictional proposal deck, without changing the original slides.

In this lab you will learn:

  • Where custom skills live in Copilot in PowerPoint
  • How to upload a skill and read what it tells Copilot to do
  • How to ask for the task without naming the skill
  • How to check the result before you rely on it

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Watch this short video first. It shows the whole lab from start to finish, using the real PowerPoint run. The video has on-screen captions and no sound.

Lab files

  • ERGO-Skill-Decision-Before.pptx - five-slide practice deck
  • ergo-decision-check.zip - the custom skill. Keep it zipped; PowerPoint reads the ZIP directly.

docs.title: Step 1: Open the practice deck
docs.text:
Upload ERGO-Skill-Decision-Before.pptx to your OneDrive and open it in PowerPoint for the web. Select Copilot on the ribbon to open the Copilot pane.

Read-only?

If PowerPoint opens the file read-only or shows a repair banner, select Save a copy and continue in the copy.

docs.title: Step 2: Open Custom skills
docs.text:
In the Copilot pane, select … (Settings and more), then Manage plugins & skills, then Custom skills. Select Add.

You will see four options: Create manually, Upload, Record a skill and Add in OneDrive.

docs.title: Step 3: Upload the skill
docs.text: Select Upload and choose ergo-decision-check.zip. Wait until ergo-decision-check appears in the list. Make sure both Custom skills and ergo-decision-check are switched on.

docs.title: Step 4: Read what the skill tells Copilot
docs.text:
Select the skill name to open it. A skill has two parts:

  • Description: when Copilot should use it. Here: decision checks, committee readiness checks or pre-meeting reviews.
  • Instructions: what Copilot must do. Here: add one Decision check slide with four sections, and never imply that funding is approved.

Close the skill panel when you are done.

docs.title: Step 1: Ask normally
docs.text:
Go to slide 4, which contains the proposal. Make sure Allow editing is on. Type this request, without selecting or naming the skill:

Do a committee readiness check.

Fresh file?

Before you ask, open Custom skills and wait until the skill appears and is switched on. If needed, select Refresh. In rehearsal, a request sent before the list had loaded produced a general review instead.

docs.title: Step 2: Review the new slide
docs.text:
Copilot adds slide 6, Decision check.

Check that the slide contains:

  • EUR 420,000, 90 days, and that funding is not yet approved
  • Finance's 15% as the base case, replacing the earlier 25% estimate
  • Missing owners or dates marked Not specified in the deck
  • Slides 1–5 unchanged

Open the speaker notes to see the source slide numbers and reasoning.

docs.title: Step 3: Ask which skill was used
docs.text:
This is optional, but useful for the group discussion.

Which custom skill did you use?

In rehearsal, Copilot answered ergo-decision-check and listed the rules it followed.

docs.title: Exercise 3: Discuss as a leader
docs.text:
Ask Copilot:

Which statement would you challenge first?

Then discuss in your group:

  • What does the committee still need before it can decide?
  • Which review in your own team is repeated often enough to become a skill?

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Copilot only replies in chat and does not add a slide

Turn on Allow editing, check that the file is not read-only and ask again.

Copilot gives a general review instead of the four-section slide

Open Custom skills, confirm both switches are on, select Refresh and wait for the skill to appear. Start a new chat and ask again. As a fallback, type @ergo-decision-check Do a committee readiness check.

The skill does not appear after upload

Select Refresh. Upload the ZIP as it is; do not unzip it first.

A Decision check slide already exists

The skill updates that slide instead of adding another. Use a fresh copy of the practice deck to see it create the slide.

Congratulations! You have completed Lab P1.

Next: Lab X1 · Excel Back to Home

docs.title: Lab X1 - Find launch blockers in a register
docs.text:
In this lab you will add a custom skill to Copilot in Excel. Then you will ask Copilot to review a fictional pilot register for launch readiness. Copilot will build a launch review with formulas you can inspect.

In this lab you will learn:

  • Where Excel stores custom skills
  • What a skill file looks like
  • How to ask for the task without naming the skill
  • How to verify the result and its formulas

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Watch this short video first. It shows the whole lab from start to finish, using the real Excel run. The video has on-screen captions and no sound.

Lab files

  • ERGO-Skill-Launch-Before.xlsx - 24-item pilot register
  • ergo-launch-review.zip - the custom skill. Unzip it: Excel reads skills from a folder named ergo-launch-review containing SKILL.md.

docs.title: Step 1: Open the practice workbook
docs.text: Upload ERGO-Skill-Launch-Before.xlsx to your OneDrive and open it in Excel for the web. Select Copilot to open the Copilot pane.

docs.title: Step 2: Open the skills folder
docs.text:
In the Copilot pane, select … (Settings and more), then Manage plugins & skills, then Custom skills. Select Add, then Add in OneDrive.

Different from PowerPoint

In this Excel version, Add offers only Add in OneDrive. If you see Create skills folder instead, select it first.

docs.title: Step 3: Upload the skill folder
docs.text:
Excel opens your OneDrive skills folder. Select Create or upload, then Folder upload, and choose the unzipped ergo-launch-review folder.

Return to Excel and select Refresh in Custom skills.

Folder, not ZIP

Upload the folder, not the ZIP. The folder name must match the skill name.

docs.title: Step 4: Read what the skill tells Copilot
docs.text:
Open SKILL.md inside the folder. The top lines tell Copilot when to use it: launch-readiness reviews, overdue action checks or owner-and-dependency reviews. The numbered rules describe how, for example:

  • Use the register's 30 September snapshot, not today's date
  • Count blocked and overdue items separately
  • Use inspectable formulas and keep the source unchanged

docs.title: Step 1: Ask normally
docs.text:
Go back to the workbook. Type this request, without selecting or naming the skill:

Review this register for launch readiness.

Copilot validates the 24 records, then builds the review. This can take a minute or two.

docs.title: Step 2: Ask which skill was used
docs.text:
Which custom skill did you use?

In rehearsal, Copilot answered ergo-launch-review.

docs.title: Step 3: Check the launch review
docs.text:
Open the new Launch review sheet.

Check Expected As of 30 Sep 2026 Total items 24 Blocked items 3: R04, A04, A08 Overdue actions 2: A03, A08

docs.title: Step 4: Inspect the formula
docs.text: Select the Overdue actions count and look at the formula bar. It counts open actions whose due date is before the snapshot date.

docs.title: Exercise 3: Discuss as a leader
docs.text:
Ask Copilot:

Why aren't all blocked items overdue?

Then discuss in your group:

  • Which overdue action would you escalate first, and to whom?
  • Which recurring check in your own area should always follow the same rules?

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
The skill does not appear in Excel

Check that you uploaded the unzipped folder and that it contains SKILL.md. Then select Refresh in Custom skills.

Copilot gives a general answer instead of a Launch review sheet

Start a new chat and ask again. As a fallback, type @ergo-launch-review Review this register for launch readiness.

The counts differ from the table

Check the reporting date in cell B2. The lab uses the register's snapshot date, 30 September 2026, not today's date.

The workbook already has a Launch review sheet

Use a fresh copy of the practice workbook so everyone starts from the same register.

Congratulations! You have completed Lab X1.

Back to Lab P1 · PowerPoint Back to Home
